title: The Watermill Center
summary: The Watermill Center is an arts residency, archive, and research library on Shinnecock ancestral territory. Jeremy Dennis developed On This Site there during a June 2017 residency, and Watermill has worked with Shinnecock artists, cultural workers, and staff including Shane Weeks, Andrina Smith, Denise Silva-Dennis, and Kelly Dennis.

history_title: On This Site and Shinnecock artists at Watermill
history_content:
The Watermill Center is an interdisciplinary arts and humanities laboratory at 39 Water Mill Towd Road, situated on ten acres of Shinnecock ancestral territory. Its campus includes studios, living spaces, an art collection, archives, and a research library.

On This Site residency and book

Shinnecock artist Jeremy Dennis was in residence from June 5 through June 16, 2017. During the residency he developed On This Site as a web map, photography project, planned book, and exhibition about Native places across Long Island. Running Strong for American Indian Youth supported the project. Dennis completed the first book edition in 2018. A copy of Edition 2 was photographed in Watermill's research library on August 30, 2023.

Shinnecock artists, staff, and collaborations

Shane Weeks joined Watermill's 2015 Flying Point residency, which created a multimedia portrait of contemporary Shinnecock life. In 2016, Kelly Dennis participated in Watermill's El Colegio del Cuerpo group with Colombian and Shinnecock performers; she later served as Public Programs and Residency Coordinator. Andrina Smith's 2019 residency developed The People of the Sandy Shore, a play about Indigenous Long Island history from colonization to the present. Watermill's education and public programs have also included Shinnecock artist and educator Denise Silva-Dennis.

At the opening of the 2021 CROSSROADS festival, Laurie Anderson, Shane Weeks, and members of the Shinnecock Nation took part in the program together. These residencies, performances, education projects, and staff roles form a continuing relationship between Watermill and Shinnecock artists and community members.
preservation_content: A copy of On This Site, Edition 2 is held in The Watermill Center research library and was photographed there in 2023. Watermill schedules public programs and campus access, so visitors interested in seeing or consulting the book should confirm current access with the Center before visiting.
